senses.sense_definition: A position that requires little to no work but provides a good salary.

examples.text: He was given a <w>sinecure</w> in the government that required him to attend only one meeting a year.
Many people believe that being a consultant for that firm is just a <w>sinecure</w> for retired politicians.

senses.sense_definition: An ecclesiastical position that does not involve the responsibility of caring for a congregation.

examples.text: The priest held a <w>sinecure</w> that allowed him to focus entirely on his historical research.
In the past, many high-ranking church officials were granted a <w>sinecure</w> to support their scholarly work.

senses.sense_definition: Requiring no work for an ample reward.

examples.text: He accepted a <w>sinecure</w> position that paid well but demanded almost no effort.
The board offered her a <w>sinecure</w> role to keep her associated with the company.

senses.sense_definition: To appoint someone to a position that requires little to no work.

examples.text: The director decided to <w>sinecure</w> his nephew in a department that had no real responsibilities.
It was common practice to <w>sinecure</w> political allies in honorary roles.
